title: Ieri e oggi
sub: Used to, would e be used to - com'era la vita prima
grammar: Used to / would per abitudini passate, be used to e get used to + -ing
situation: Parlare con il padrone di casa: affitto e guasti

lessons.title: Used to, would, be used to
lessons.intro: In italiano usiamo l'imperfetto per tutto: «giocavo», «ero abituato». In inglese servono tre strutture diverse, e gli italiani le confondono di continuo. Qui impari quando usare ciascuna.

steps.title: Used to: abitudini e stati che non esistono più
steps.body:
**Used to + verbo base** descrive qualcosa di **vero in passato ma non più oggi**: un'abitudine ripetuta o uno stato.
- I **used to play** football every day. (ora non più)
- We **used to live** in Naples. (ora abitiamo altrove)

Negativa e domanda: **didn't use to** / **Did you use to...?** Con did la -d sparisce, perché il passato è già nell'ausiliare.

Non si usa per fatti passati unici o con una durata precisa: «I lived in Rome for five years» (non «I used to live for five years»).

**Errori tipici**: «I used to going», «I didn't used to like it», «I use to play».
table: She used to have long hair.
We didn't use to have a car.
Did you use to walk to school?
ex: I used to be afraid of dogs.
Ero spaventato dai cani (adesso no).
Did you use to read comics as a child?
Da piccolo leggevi i fumetti?
My parents didn't use to let me stay out late.
I miei genitori non mi lasciavano rientrare tardi.

steps.title: Would: solo per azioni ripetute
steps.body:
**Would + verbo base** si usa per le **azioni ripetute** del passato, quando il contesto (spesso un'espressione di tempo) è già chiaro:
- Every summer we **would go** to my grandparents' farm.
- On Sundays my father **would make** pancakes.

Ma **non** si usa per gli **stati** (be, have, like, know, live, believe): «I would be shy» è sbagliato; si dice **I used to be shy**.

Si inizia di solito con **used to** per fissare il periodo, poi si continua con **would** per i dettagli:
«We **used to** spend every summer at the lake. We **would** get up early and swim before breakfast.»
ex: When I was little, I would spend hours drawing.
Da piccolo passavo ore a disegnare.
I used to have a dog. He would wait for me at the gate every afternoon.
Avevo un cane. Mi aspettava al cancello ogni pomeriggio.

steps.title: Be used to e get used to: essere abituati / abituarsi
steps.body:
Qui **to è una preposizione**, quindi dopo ci va un **nome o la forma in -ing**, mai il verbo base.
- **be used to + -ing**: essere abituato. I'**m used to getting up** early.
- **get used to + -ing**: abituarsi (il processo). It took me a month to **get used to working** nights.
- Passato: I **wasn't used to** the cold. / In the end, I **got used to** it.

Non confonderle con **used to + base** (abitudine passata): «I used to live in London» ma «I'm used to living in London».

**Errori tipici**: «I'm not used to wake up early», «I get used to drive on the left» (manca l'-ing).
ex: I'm not used to this weather.
Non sono abituato a questo clima.
She's slowly getting used to living alone.
Si sta pian piano abituando a vivere da sola.

steps.title: Quale scegliere? Un riassunto
steps.body:
- Una **serie di momenti**, un periodo concluso, ora non più vero: **used to**.
- Un'azione ripetuta con dettagli narrativi: **would** (mai con stati).
- Un fatto isolato o con durata esatta: **past simple** (I lived there for ten years).
- «Sono abituato» o «mi sto abituando»: **be / get used to + -ing**.

Se vuoi dire che qualcosa è ancora vero oggi usa il **present simple**: «I live in Turin», non «I used to live in Turin».
ex: I used to smoke, but I stopped five years ago.
Fumavo, ma ho smesso cinque anni fa.
I've lived here for years, so I'm used to the traffic.
Vivo qui da anni, quindi sono abituato al traffico.

steps.s: When I was a child, we ___ to the seaside every August.
steps.it: Da bambini andavamo al mare ogni agosto.
steps.why: Abitudine passata: used to + verbo base. «Use to» è per le frasi con did; «used to going» è un errore da -ing.

steps.s: I didn't ___ like vegetables, but now I eat them every day.
steps.why: Dopo didn't la forma è use to, senza -d.

steps.s: Did you ___ play outside every afternoon?
steps.why: Nelle domande con did: use to, senza -d.

steps.s: My grandfather ___ tell us stories every evening.
steps.why: Azione ripetuta in passato: would. «Be used to» significa «essere abituato», un altro significato.

steps.s: I ___ a very shy boy, but I'm much more confident now.
steps.why: «Be» è un verbo di stato: con gli stati si usa used to, non would.

steps.s: I'm not used to ___ so early; I'm normally a night owl.
steps.why: Dopo be used to ci vuole la forma in -ing, perché to è una preposizione.

steps.s: It took me months to get used to ___ on the left in England.
steps.why: Get used to + -ing.

opts: We used to live in a flat near the station.
We would live in a flat near the station.
We were used to live in a flat near the station.
steps.why: Live è uno stato e qui non c'è azione ripetuta: used to. «Were used to live» è un errore tipico.

steps.q: Quale frase significa «Ormai sono abituato al rumore»?
opts: I'm used to the noise now.
I used to the noise now.
I use to the noise now.
steps.why: «Essere abituato» = be used to + nome o -ing.

steps.q: Usa used to con il verbo tra parentesi
steps.s: She ___ (have) long hair, but she cut it last year.
answers: used to have
steps.why: Stato passato che non è più vero: used to + have.

steps.q: Forma negativa con didn't + il verbo tra parentesi
steps.s: We ___ (eat) fast food when I was a kid.
answers: didn't use to eat
did not use to eat
steps.why: Negativa: didn't use to + base, senza -d.

steps.q: Completa con le due parole giuste (live)
steps.s: At first I wasn't used ___ in a big city.
answers: to living
steps.why: Be used to + -ing.

steps.s: I didn't used to like coffee.
answers: I didn't use to like coffee
I did not use to like coffee
steps.why: Con did la forma è use to: la -d sparisce.

steps.s: I'm not used to wake up so early.
answers: I'm not used to waking up so early
I am not used to waking up so early
steps.why: Dopo be used to ci vuole -ing.

steps.s: When I was young, I would be very thin.
answers: When I was young, I used to be very thin
When I was young, I was very thin
steps.why: Be è un verbo di stato: non si usa would.

steps.s1: I played the piano every day when I was a child, but I don't now.
steps.s2: I ___ the piano every day when I was a child.
answers: used to play
steps.why: Abitudine passata che non c'è più: used to + base.

steps.s1: Driving on the left is still strange for me.
answers: used to driving
steps.why: Be used to + -ing.

steps.it: Quando ero piccolo passavamo ogni estate in montagna.
steps.en: When I was little we used to spend every summer in the mountains
alts: We used to spend every summer in the mountains when I was little

lessons.title: Crescere e cambiare
lessons.intro: Il lessico per raccontare l'infanzia, la famiglia e come sono cambiate le cose. Include phrasal verbs molto usati quando si parla di famiglia e di scuola.

ex: I had a happy childhood in a small town.
Ho avuto un'infanzia felice in una piccola città.
She had a strict upbringing.
Ha avuto un'educazione severa.
words.note: Non è l'istruzione scolastica (education) né la buona educazione (manners).

ex: Our teacher was very strict about homework.
La nostra insegnante era molto severa sui compiti.
words.note: «Severe» in inglese è molto più forte: si usa per tempeste o malattie.

ex: We met in the school playground every break.
Ci trovavamo nel cortile della scuola a ogni intervallo.
I got five pounds pocket money a week.
Ricevevo cinque sterline di paghetta a settimana.
I grew up in a village near Siena.
Sono cresciuto in un paese vicino a Siena.
words.note: Si riferisce a chi cresce: «crescere» un figlio è bring up.

ex: She was brought up by her grandparents.
È stata cresciuta dai nonni.
words.note: Spesso al passivo: be brought up.

ex: My teacher told me off for talking in class.
L'insegnante mi ha rimproverato perché parlavo in classe.
words.note: Si dice tell somebody off (for something); spesso al passivo: be told off.

ex: When I look back on my school years, I smile.
Quando ripenso agli anni di scuola, sorrido.
Old photos make my grandmother nostalgic.
Le vecchie foto rendono nostalgica mia nonna.
words.note: Di solito: nostalgic about / for something.

ex: My grandfather has some old-fashioned ideas.
Mio nonno ha qualche idea all'antica.
My grandparents' generation didn't travel much.
La generazione dei miei nonni viaggiava poco.
Biting your nails is a bad habit.
Mangiarsi le unghie è una cattiva abitudine.
words.note: Si dice get into the habit of + -ing; «abitudine» come usanza collettiva è custom.

ex: A healthy lifestyle means sleeping well.
Uno stile di vita sano significa dormire bene.

steps.s: The teacher always ___ us off if we forgot our homework.
steps.why: Il phrasal verb è tell somebody off (rimproverare); say e speak non formano questa espressione.

steps.s: My parents were quite ___: we had to be home by nine, even at weekends.
steps.why: Per genitori o insegnanti rigidi si dice strict; severe è molto più forte.

steps.s: When I ___ back on my school years, I feel a bit nostalgic.
answers: look
steps.why: Look back on = ripensare a.

steps.s: My grandmother gets very ___ when she sees old photos.
answers: nostalgic
steps.why: Serve un aggettivo: nostalgia -> nostalgic.

steps.s: Young people today have a different attitude to work from my grandparents' ___ .
answers: generation
steps.why: Serve un nome: generate -> generation.

steps.q: Che cosa significa «She was brought up by her aunt»?
opts: È stata cresciuta da sua zia.
È stata portata su da sua zia.
steps.why: Be brought up = essere cresciuto, allevato da qualcuno.

lessons.title: Estati senza schermi
lessons.intro: Un articolo in cui un genitore confronta le sue estati di bambino con quelle delle sue figlie. Fai attenzione a come usa used to e would per il passato.

steps.title: Summers without screens
steps.text:
When I was a child in the late 1990s, my summers always followed the same pattern. As soon as school finished in June, my cousins and I would spend the whole day outside. We used to meet at the playground behind my grandmother's building at nine o'clock, and we didn't come home until it got dark. Nobody had a mobile phone, so my mother simply used to shout from the balcony when lunch was ready.

Of course, we weren't always angels. We would borrow our neighbours' bicycles without asking, and one summer we built a wooden hut in a field, which collapsed after three days. My grandfather, who was quite strict, used to make us repair everything we broke. At the time I hated it. Now I think it taught me more than any school lesson.

Last month I took my own daughters, aged nine and twelve, to the same playground. It was almost empty. They weren't used to playing outside without a tablet in their hands, and for the first ten minutes they complained that they were bored. Then something changed. A boy arrived with a football, and soon there were six children running around and shouting, just like in my day.

I'm not saying that technology is a problem. My daughters can do things I could never do at their age: they edit videos, they speak to friends in other countries and they learn English from online games. But I would like them to have some of my memories too. So we have made a new rule: every Saturday morning, the phones stay at home and we go to the park.

It wasn't easy at first. My elder daughter got really angry the first week, but now she has got used to it, and last Saturday she was the one who reminded me to leave my phone on the table. Perhaps every generation looks back on its childhood with a little nostalgia. The important thing is to make sure that the new generation has something to be nostalgic about, too.

qs.q: What did the writer's mother do when lunch was ready?
qs.why: «My mother simply used to shout from the balcony when lunch was ready».

qs.q: What happened to the hut the children built?
opts: It fell down after a few days.
It stayed in the field for years.

qs.q: How does the writer feel now about the grandfather's rule?
qs.why: «At the time I hated it. Now I think it taught me more than any school lesson.»

qs.q: The playground was crowded when the writer took the daughters there.
The daughters weren't used to playing outside without a ___ .
answers: tablet

qs.q: Why does the writer mention that the daughters edit videos?
opts: To show that technology has positive sides.
To complain about their screen time.
To say that they are cleverer than their parents.
qs.why: «I'm not saying that technology is a problem. My daughters can do things I could never do...»

qs.q: What is the new family rule?
opts: The phones stay at home on Saturday mornings.
The girls can't use tablets at all.
They go to the park every day.
qs.why: «Every Saturday morning, the phones stay at home and we go to the park.»

qs.q: The younger daughter found the new rule difficult.
qs.why: Si parla solo della figlia maggiore (elder daughter).

steps.q: Nel testo, «she has got used to it» significa:
steps.why: Have got used to = essersi abituati.

steps.s: The wooden hut ___ after only three days.
steps.why: Collapse = crollare. Collect e cancel hanno altri significati.

lessons.title: Un italiano in Scozia
lessons.intro: Un'intervista radiofonica con un uomo che si è trasferito dall'Italia alla Scozia. Ascolta come racconta le abitudini di prima e quelle di adesso.

steps.title: Life Stories
steps.it: Ascolta l'intervista e rispondi. Puoi riascoltarla e usare la velocità lenta.
lines: Welcome back to Life Stories. Today I'm talking to Marco, who moved from Turin to Scotland ten years ago. Marco, was it difficult at first?
Oh, very. The weather was the first shock. In Turin we used to have long, hot summers, and here it rains almost every day. I just wasn't used to it.

Well, I used to eat dinner at nine o'clock. Here everybody has dinner at six! At the beginning I was starving at five, and then I couldn't sleep because I had eaten so much so late. Now I'm used to it, but I still cook pasta on Sundays, and my neighbours love it.

School, actually. My son was seven when we arrived. In Italy he used to have lessons in the morning and then go home for lunch, but in Glasgow he stayed at school until half past three. He hated it for the first month. Then he made friends, and now he says he would never go back.
And you? Would you go back?

Honestly, I don't know. I miss my family, of course. We used to meet every Sunday for lunch at my grandmother's, and I miss that tradition. But I've got a good job here, and I've got used to the Scottish accent, which was the hardest thing of all! Now I can understand almost everybody, even the taxi drivers.
Thank you, Marco, and good luck.

qs.q: What was the first thing Marco found difficult?
At the beginning, Marco was hungry at ___ o'clock.
answers: five

qs.q: How did Marco's son feel about school at first?
opts: He was afraid of the teachers.

qs.q: What was the hardest thing for Marco?

steps.en: We used to meet every Sunday for lunch at my grandmother's.
steps.it: Ci trovavamo ogni domenica a pranzo da mia nonna.

steps.en: It took me a long time to get used to the accent.
steps.it: Mi ci è voluto molto tempo per abituarmi all'accento.

steps.en: I used to live in a small town, but now I'm used to the city.
steps.it: Vivevo in una piccola città, ma ora sono abituato alla grande città.

lessons.title: Dal padrone di casa
lessons.intro: Il riscaldamento si rompe, l'affitto è in ritardo: come parlare con il landlord in modo chiaro ma educato. In inglese il tono fa la differenza.

steps.title: Segnalare un guasto
steps.body:
Il proprietario si chiama **landlord** (o **landlady**), l'inquilino **tenant**. Non esiste «the owner» in questo senso.
- **I'm calling about** the flat at 12 Park Road.
- **The heating isn't working** / **The tap is leaking** / **There's a problem with the boiler.**
- **It's been like that since Monday.**
- **I've already checked** the thermostat.
- **Could you send someone to take a look?**
- **When would be convenient for you?**

Si descrive il problema (cosa non funziona), si dice da quando, e poi si chiede una soluzione con **Could you...?**
ex: The shower isn't draining properly.
La doccia non scarica bene.
Could you send someone to take a look?
Potrebbe mandare qualcuno a dare un'occhiata?

steps.title: Registro: troppo diretto o giusto?
steps.body:
Con il padrone di casa meglio un tono cortese, anche se sei arrabbiato.
- Troppo diretto: «You must fix it today.» / «Pay me now.»
- Giusto: **Would it be possible to...?** / **I was wondering if you could...** / **I'm afraid that...**

Per chiedere un favore sull'affitto: **Would it be possible to pay the rent a few days late?** Per promettere: **It won't happen again.** Per ringraziare: **I really appreciate it** (non «you are very gentle»: gentle = delicato).
ex: I was wondering if you could repair the window.
Mi chiedevo se potesse riparare la finestra.
I'm afraid I won't be home on Thursday morning.
Temo di non essere a casa giovedì mattina.

steps.title: Il riscaldamento non funziona
steps.it: Scegli la battuta più naturale e cortese (Tu).

opts: Hello, Mr Hughes. This is Elena Rossi from flat 3. I'm calling because the heating isn't working.
Hello, Mr Hughes. I'm Elena of flat 3, the heating not works and I want that you fix it today.
Hello, Mr Hughes. You must fix the heating immediately, it is your duty.

lines: I'm sorry to hear that. How long has it been like that?

opts: Since Monday. I've already checked the thermostat and the batteries.
From Monday. I already check the thermostat.
Since Monday. I am checking the thermostat since yesterday.

lines: I'll send an engineer. Would Thursday morning be convenient?

opts: I'm afraid I'll be at work on Thursday morning. Would the afternoon be possible?
No, Thursday is impossible, you must come on Friday.
Thursday not go well for me, come another day.

steps.why: In inglese si propone un'alternativa con «Would ... be possible?»; «since» + momento di inizio si usa con il present perfect, non con il present simple.

steps.title: Un po' di ritardo con l'affitto
lines: Hello Elena, what can I do for you?

opts: I wanted to ask if it would be possible to pay this month's rent a few days late.
I tell you that this month I pay the rent late, ok?
Would be possible that I will pay you the rent after.

lines: That's not something I usually accept. What's the problem?

opts: My salary will arrive on the 8th instead of the 1st. It won't happen again.
My salary come late, it is not my fault, so you accept.
I have not money now, you wait.

lines: All right. As long as I get it by the 10th, that's fine.

opts: Thank you very much, I really appreciate it.

steps.why: «Gentle» è un falso amico: significa «delicato». Per ringraziare di una cortesia si dice «I really appreciate it».

pairs: Could you send someone to take a look?
Potrebbe mandare qualcuno a dare un'occhiata?
The rent is due on the first of the month.
L'affitto va pagato il primo del mese.
I'd like to get my deposit back.

steps.it: Sarebbe possibile pagare l'affitto con qualche giorno di ritardo?
steps.en: Would it be possible to pay the rent a few days late
Hello, it's Anna from flat 4. The boiler has stopped working.
steps.it: Buongiorno, sono Anna dell'appartamento 4. La caldaia ha smesso di funzionare.

steps.en: Would it be possible to send someone tomorrow morning?
steps.it: Sarebbe possibile mandare qualcuno domani mattina?

steps.en: I'd like to know when I'll get my deposit back.
steps.it: Vorrei sapere quando riavrò la caparra.

steps.q: You phone your landlord because there is a problem in your flat. Explain it and ask for help.
steps.it: Telefona al padrone di casa: spiega il problema, da quando c'è, cosa hai già provato e proponi un giorno per la riparazione (almeno 5 frasi, tono cortese).
hints: The ... isn't working. It's been like that since...
steps.model: Hello, Mrs Brown, it's Luca from flat 6. I'm calling about the washing machine. It isn't working and it's been like that since Tuesday. I've already checked the plug and the filter, but nothing has changed. Could you send someone to take a look? I'm at home on Friday morning, so would that be convenient for you? Thank you, I really appreciate it.

lessons.title: Come è cambiata la mia vita
lessons.intro: Scriverai un breve articolo per una rivista, confrontando com'eri prima e come sei adesso. Prima prepari struttura, connettivi e strutture grammaticali.

steps.title: Come si scrive un articolo
steps.body:
Un articolo ha **un titolo**, un'introduzione che cattura il lettore e **2-3 paragrafi** con una chiusura personale. Il tono è semi-informale: si possono usare contrazioni e domande.

**Connettivi utili**:
- passato: **When I was..., Back then, Ten years ago**
- presente: **These days, Nowadays, Now**
- contrasto: **However, Although, but**
- conclusione: **All in all, To sum up**

**Trucco**: apri con used to per fissare il periodo, poi usa would per i dettagli (ma solo con azioni, non stati) e passa al presente con These days.
ex: Ten years ago I used to get up at seven.
Dieci anni fa mi alzavo alle sette.
These days I'm used to working from home.
Oggi sono abituato a lavorare da casa.

steps.s: I used to be shy. ___, these days I enjoy talking to new people.
steps.why: Contrasto tra due frasi: However, con la virgola. Although introduce una subordinata nella stessa frase.

steps.s: ___ I was a teenager, I used to read for hours every evening.
steps.why: Dopo la congiunzione segue una frase intera: When. During vuole un nome.

steps.s: Ten years ago I used to living in a village.
answers: Ten years ago I used to live in a village
Ten years ago I lived in a village
steps.why: Used to vuole il verbo base, non -ing.

steps.s1: I don't go to the cinema every week now, but I did in the past.
steps.s2: I ___ to the cinema every week.
answers: used to go
steps.why: Abitudine passata: used to + base.

steps.q: You see this notice in an English-language magazine: Articles wanted for our series 'How my life has changed'. Write your article. Say what you used to do, what is different now, and which change you like most.
steps.it: Scrivi un articolo dal titolo «How my life has changed»: cosa facevi prima, cosa è diverso adesso e quale cambiamento preferisci. Usa un titolo e 2-3 paragrafi.
checklist: Ho messo un titolo e organizzato il testo in paragrafi
Ho usato almeno due volte used to + verbo base
Ho usato almeno una volta be used to o get used to + -ing
Ho usato connettivi come however, these days, although
Ho detto quale cambiamento preferisco e perché
useful: Ten years ago I used to...
At first I wasn't used to...
steps.model:
How my life has changed

Ten years ago I was a student in a small town. I used to get up at seven, walk to school and spend every afternoon playing football with my friends. We didn't have smartphones, so we would simply knock on each other's doors.

These days everything is different. I live in a big city and I work in an office. At first I wasn't used to the noise and the crowds, but now I love the energy. I don't play football any more, although I sometimes join a team on Sundays.

Of course, I miss my old friends. However, the change has been good for me: I've become more independent, and I'm proud of that.

steps.q: Describe a place you loved as a child.
steps.it: Descrivi un posto che amavi da bambino: dov'era, cosa facevi lì, come ti sentivi (almeno 4 frasi con used to o would).
hints: When I was a child, I used to...
steps.model: When I was a child, I used to spend every summer at my grandparents' house near the sea. We would get up early and go to the beach before breakfast. In the afternoon my grandfather would tell us stories under the fig tree. I remember the smell of the sea and the sound of the cicadas. These days the house belongs to my uncle, but I still feel nostalgic every time I pass it.

steps.q: Talk about something you had to get used to when you moved or started a new job.
steps.it: Parla di qualcosa a cui hai dovuto abituarti dopo un cambiamento (una nuova città, un lavoro, un orario).
hints: When I started..., I wasn't used to...
It took me ... to get used to...
steps.model: When I started my new job, I wasn't used to getting up at six. It took me about a month to get used to the early start. The hardest thing was the commute, because I used to live five minutes from my old office. Now I'm used to reading on the train, and I actually enjoy the quiet time.

lessons.title: Test dell'unità 3
lessons.intro: Verifica senza aiuti: used to, would, be used to e il lessico dell'infanzia e dei cambiamenti. Le correzioni le vedi alla fine.

steps.s: We ___ to my grandparents' house every Sunday when I was little.
Where did you ___ live before you moved here?
Our teacher ___ give us a lot of homework on Fridays.
I can't get used to ___ on the left side of the road.
My sister ___ very quiet, but now she never stops talking.
I'm not used to ___ so much noise at night.
My parents were very ___ and never let us stay out late.
My teacher ___ me off for arriving late three times.

opts: I didn't use to like jazz.
I didn't used to like jazz.
I not used to like jazz.

steps.q: Quale frase significa «Mi sto abituando al nuovo orario»?
opts: I'm getting used to the new timetable.
I'm using to the new timetable.
I'm used to get the new timetable.

steps.s: I grew ___ in a small village near Siena.
answers: up

steps.q: Usa used to con il verbo live
steps.s: We ___ in a flat above a bakery when I was a child.
answers: used to live

steps.text: Non sono abituato a lavorare di notte.
answers: I'm not used to working at night
I am not used to working at night
I'm not used to working nights
I am not used to working nights
I'm not used to working during the night
I am not used to working during the night
